title: IAHR-APD Annual Report 2024
summary: The Division's report to the IAHR Council for 2024.

body.text: Including but not limited to conferences, webinars, publications, working meetings, elections, participation in international processes, etc. Some examples below:
24th IAHR-APD Congress – “Water for a Changing Future”

items: Jointly organized by the Changjiang River Scientific Research Institute (CRSRI) & Sichuan Univ.
> 500 participants from 30 + countries (gov’t, IOs, academia, industry, students).
Eight sub-themes ranging from hazard-risk reduction to smart-water tech & estuarine/coastal engineering.
500 + abstracts → 230 full papers accepted (recommended for Scopus).
12 special sessions & 4 side events; technical & post-conference tours (Three Gorges Dam, Dujiangyan, Giant Panda Base, etc.).
Heritage nomination: Hankou Hydrological Station (1865).
Advanced regional cooperation toward the UN SDGs.
First fully face-to-face EC since the pandemic; 11 / 15 members (> 73 %) present, co-chaired by Prof. Norio Tanaka (Chair) & Dr. Won Kim (Secretary).
Reviewed 2023–24 APD activities & finances; endorsed 25th & 26th Congress hosts; approved by-law amendments (Executive Committee size, YPN seat, Secretariat rules).
Recorded in official minutes for transparency & archival.

body.text: Continues joint publication (Elsevier) with KWRA & IAHR-APD.

items: 2018-23: 2 462 submissions → 556 sent to review; 39 % acceptance.
2023 Impact Factor = 2.470 (steady rise).
Emphasis on rapid, high-quality eco-hydraulics & water-resources research; global authorship.

body.text: Awarded to Dr. Gregory Shahane De Costa (Open Polytechnic NZ) for decades-long contributions (APD VP 2014-18, President 2018-22; Congress chair 2010 & 2016).

items: Cited for advancing hydro-environmental collaboration across APD.

25th IAHR-APD Congress – “Hydro-environments in the Era of Climate Change and AI”

items: LOC chaired by Prof. Sung-Uk Choi (Yonsei Univ.)
Grand ballroom (3 000 pax) + 35 rooms, 900-booth hall.
Five keynote speeches; ≈ 10 special sessions; SCI-indexed special issues.
Call for abstracts opens 1 Jul 2025; full papers due 1 Apr 2026.
Master classes (2), Best Paper Awards, video-poster sessions, tech exhibition.
Technical tours: Gunnam Dam, ARA Waterway, Cheonggye-cheon, Han River.
Target 320 – 400 participants.

body.text: 26th IAHR-APD Congress – “He Tāonga te Wai – Water is a Treasure”

items: Joint hosts: Open Polytechnic NZ & Victoria Univ. of Wellington.
Five-day programme: pre-workshops, technical sessions, dinner, visits.
Compact walkable CBD venues (James Cook Hotel & VUW).
Late-summer climate; easy intl. access.
Engagement with NZ Hydrological Society, NZ Society on Large Dams, Coastal Soc., Meteorological Soc.
